    private enum class Dir { UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT }
    private enum class State { RUNNING, PAUSED, GAME_OVER }

    private data class Cell(val x: Int, val y: Int)

    companion object {
        private const val COLS = 22
        private const val BASE_DELAY = 320L
        private const val MIN_DELAY = 80L

    private var best = 0
    private var state = State.PAUSED
    private var startTime = 0L

    private val handler = Handler(Looper.getMainLooper())
    private val tick = object : Runnable {
        override fun run() {
            if (state == State.RUNNING) {
                step()
                invalidate()
                handler.postDelayed(this, currentDelay())
            }
        }
    }

```kotlin
private fun step() {
    dir = pendingDir
    val head = snake[0]
    val nh = when (dir) {
        Dir.UP -> Cell(head.x, head.y - 1)
        Dir.DOWN -> Cell(head.x, head.y + 1)
        Dir.LEFT -> Cell(head.x - 1, head.y)
        Dir.RIGHT -> Cell(head.x + 1, head.y)
    }
    if (nh.x < 0 || nh.x >= COLS || nh.y < 0 || nh.y >= rows || snake.contains(nh)) {
        gameOver()
        return
    }
    snake.add(0, nh)
    if (nh == food) {
        score++
        if (score > best) { best = score; saveBest() }
        spawnFood()
        blip? (no sound needed)
    } else {
        snake.removeAt(snake.size - 1)
    }
}
```

Note: classic snake allows moving into the cell the tail just vacated. snake.contains(nh) check happens before tail removal, so moving into the tail's current cell counts as collision even though it would vacate. Touch handling:
```kotlin
private var downX = 0f
private var downY = 0f

override fun onTouchEvent(event: MotionEvent): Boolean {
    when (event.action) {
        MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN -> {
            downX = event.x; downY = event.y
            if (state == State.GAME_OVER) { reset(); invalidate(); handler.post(tick)... }
            else if (state == State.PAUSED) { resume }
            return true
        }
        MotionEvent.ACTION_UP -> {
            val dx = event.x - downX
            val dy = event.y - downY
            val minSwipe = resources.displayMetrics.density * 24
            if (state == State.RUNNING && (abs(dx) > minSwipe || abs(dy) > minSwipe)) {
                if (abs(dx) >= abs(dy)) setDir(if (dx > 0) Dir.RIGHT else Dir.LEFT)
                else setDir(if (dy > 0) Dir.DOWN else Dir.UP)
            }
            return true
        }
    }
    return super.onTouchEvent(event)
}

private fun setDir(d: Dir) {
    // prevent reversing
    val opposite = (dir == Dir.UP && d == Dir.DOWN) || ...
    // better: prevent reversing relative to current actual dir
    if (!isOpposite(d, dir)) pendingDir = d
}
```

Also prevent double-turn within one tick causing self-collision (e.g., quickly UP then LEFT while moving RIGHT — pendingDir=UP then LEFT is fine; but RIGHT then quickly DOWN+LEFT: pending DOWN then LEFT — LEFT is opposite of RIGHT, but dir is already... at next tick dir becomes pending. If user swipes DOWN then LEFT quickly, pending becomes LEFT while dir still RIGHT → isOpposite(LEFT, RIGHT) → ignored? isOpposite checks against current dir (RIGHT), so LEFT ignored; but after tick dir=DOWN... the LEFT swipe was lost. Acceptable for casual game. Better approach: check opposite against pendingDir too:

```kotlin
private fun setDir(d: Dir) {
    val ref = pendingDir
    if (!isOpposite(d, ref) && d != ref) pendingDir = d
}
```

Hmm, if dir=RIGHT, pending=DOWN (already swiped), then swipe LEFT: ref=DOWN, LEFT not opposite of DOWN → pending=LEFT. Next tick: dir=LEFT while body heading RIGHT → instant self collision? Head at (x,y) moving left into segment at (x-1,y)? The second segment is at (x-1,y) indeed since we were moving right. So that's a death. The classic fix: only allow one direction change per tick, or validate against the direction that will be current. Simplest robust: check against `dir` (last applied) and also disallow opposite of dir: LEFT vs dir=RIGHT → ignored. So check against dir only. The loss of quick double-swipe is acceptable. Actually a small input queue is the nicest, but keep simple: check against pendingDir but ALSO ensure not opposite to dir:

```kotlin
private fun setDir(d: Dir) {
    if (isOpposite(d, dir)) return
    pendingDir = d
}
```

With dir=RIGHT, swipe DOWN (pending=DOWN), then swipe LEFT → isOpposite(LEFT, dir=RIGHT) → return. Good. Swipe DOWN then UP → isOpposite(UP, RIGHT)? no → pending=UP; tick: dir=UP, moving up from a right-moving snake — legal (no collision since up cell is free unless something there). Fine.

fun pauseGame() {

private fun startGame() {
    snake.clear()
    val cy = rows / 2
    val cx = cols / 2
    snake.add(Cell(cx, cy))
    snake.add(Cell(cx - 1, cy))
    snake.add(Cell(cx - 2, cy))
    dir = Dir.RIGHT
    pendingDir = Dir.RIGHT
    score = 0
    startedAt = System.currentTimeMillis()
    spawnFood()
    state = State.RUNNING
    handler.removeCallbacks(ticker)
    handler.post(ticker)
    invalidate()
}

spawnFood():
```kotlin
private fun spawnFood() {
    val free = ArrayList<Cell>()
    for (y in 0 until rows) for (x in 0 until cols) {
        val c = Cell(x, y)
        if (!snake.contains(c)) free.add(c)
    }
    if (free.isEmpty()) { gameOver(); return }
    food = free[Random.nextInt(free.size)]
}
```

step():
```kotlin
private fun step() {
    dir = pendingDir
    val head = snake[0]
    val next = when (dir) {
        Dir.UP -> Cell(head.x, head.y - 1)
        Dir.DOWN -> Cell(head.x, head.y + 1)
        Dir.LEFT -> Cell(head.x - 1, head.y)
        Dir.RIGHT -> Cell(head.x + 1, head.y)
    }
    if (next.x < 0 || next.x >= cols || next.y < 0 || next.y >= rows) { gameOver(); return }
    val grows = next == food
    val limit = if (grows) snake.size else snake.size - 1
    for (i in 0 until limit) if (snake[i] == next) { gameOver(); return }
    snake.add(0, next)
    if (grows) {
        score++
        if (score > best) { best = score; prefs.edit().putInt("best", best).apply() }
        spawnFood()
        performHapticFeedback(HapticFeedbackConstants.KEYBOARD_TAP)
    } else {
        snake.removeAt(snake.size - 1)
    }
}
```

private var downX = 0f
private var downY = 0f

override fun onTouchEvent(event: MotionEvent): Boolean {
    when (event.actionMasked) {
        MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN -> {
            downX = event.x
            downY = event.y
            when (state) {
                State.GAME_OVER -> startGame()
                State.PAUSED -> resumeGame()
                else -> {}
            }
            return true
        }
        MotionEvent.ACTION_UP -> {
            if (state == State.RUNNING) {
                val dx = event.x - downX
                val dy = event.y - downY
                val minSwipe = density * 20
                if (abs(dx) >= minSwipe || abs(dy) >= minSwipe) {
                    if (abs(dx) >= abs(dy)) steer(if (dx > 0) Dir.RIGHT else Dir.LEFT)
                    else steer(if (dy > 0) Dir.DOWN else Dir.UP)
                }
            }
            return true
        }
    }
    return super.onTouchEvent(event)
}

private fun steer(d: Dir) {
    val opposite = when (dir) {
        Dir.UP -> d == Dir.DOWN
        Dir.DOWN -> d == Dir.UP
        Dir.LEFT -> d == Dir.RIGHT
        Dir.RIGHT -> d == Dir.LEFT
    }
    if (!opposite) pendingDir = d
}

private fun blend(c1: Int, c2: Int, f: Float): Int {
    val r = Color.red(c1) + ((Color.red(c2) - Color.red(c1)) * f).toInt()
    val g = Color.green(c1) + ((Color.green(c2) - Color.green(c1)) * f).toInt()
    val b = Color.blue(c1) + ((Color.blue(c2) - Color.blue(c1)) * f).toInt()
    return Color.rgb(r, g, b)
}

**What I built:** A complete, dependency-free Snake game in Kotlin (package `com.example.snake`, AGP 8.7.3 + Kotlin 2.0.21, minSdk 24 / targetSdk 35).

- **Controls:** Swipe detection on the dominant axis (with 180°-turn protection); tap to pause/resume and restart.
- **Gameplay:** Classic grid-based movement, wall/self collision → game over, food growth, and a tick delay that shrinks with both score and elapsed time (`320ms → 80ms` floor), so speed ramps up as you play.
- **Extras:** Best score persisted via SharedPreferences, haptic feedback on eat/death, "Swipe to steer" hint, fullscreen Material theme, portrait-locked activity, and a vector launcher icon.
- **Structure:** `MainActivity` hosts the view and pauses/resumes the game loop (Handler-based) with the activity lifecycle.
